name: Industrious Labs (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: by share of the result's parts at the defaults, harms and goods alike. The rules' compliance costs and the deaths their cleaner air avoids (nearly all of the size) fall in the United States; the tonnes' heat deaths are spread by world population.
summary: Industrious Labs (Cincinnati) campaigns to cut emissions from US heavy industry: steel, aluminium, cement, industrial heat and landfills. This model counts the four rules it helped win in 2023-2024 (South Coast AQMD's Rules 1146.2 for water heaters, boilers and pool heaters and 1153.1 for commercial ovens, and EPA's 2024 steel-mill and coke-oven air-toxics rules), with its lost steel and aluminium campaigns at zero, against its spending in those years (about $3.7 million a year, from Tides Foundation's grants to it; its own accounts aren't public). At the defaults the rules' compliance costs (the regulators' own figures) outweigh their tonnes and the deaths and illness their cleaner air avoids in the Los Angeles basin, a small net harm of about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000: the heat-pump rule's costs exceed its benefits by about a third, and the oven rule's higher electricity bills are several times its health benefit. The sign turns on the discount rate, the heat pumps' real cost and how far the district's per-unit energy use holds. Every branch is discounted for missing data: nothing is measured for its work.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Air pollution these tonnes carry
sections.explainer: Every tonne avoids its heat deaths; a tonne from burning less fossil fuel near people also avoids air-pollution deaths. These rows say how much of the shared air-pollution rate applies to this charity's tonnes (docs/normalization.md 2.5); the rates themselves stay shared.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in tonnes
sections.explainer: The won rules' local health effects and compliance costs (units of value) enter the tonnes only through the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6).

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

Rule 1146.2 (water heaters, boilers, pool heaters; June 2024): tonnes of CO₂ a year averted once fully in effect
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate, 2.2 million tonnes, 1.4 to 2.5): gas no longer burned by about 1.07 million units in the Los Angeles basin, less the power their heat pumps draw, from the district's per-unit energy figures.

rows.label: Rule 1153.1 (commercial food ovens; August 2023): tonnes of CO₂ a year averted once fully in effect
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate, {{row:s53_tco2_per_year}} tonnes, −15,000 to 26,000): electric ovens in about 100 bakeries and food plants, net of the power they draw; on a gas-fired grid they could add emissions.

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: tonnes of CO₂e a year, upstream methane included
rows.explainer: Gas not burned is also gas not leaked upstream: combustion CO₂ grossed up by the methane share (conversion section).

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: tonnes of CO₂e a year, upstream methane included
rows.explainer: As for Rule 1146.2.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e a year the period's won rules would avert once in effect
rows.explainer: The two South Coast rules; EPA's two steel air-toxics rules cut no greenhouse gas (their health effects are counted below).

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: early deaths a year avoided by its NOx cut, once fully in effect
rows.explainer: The district's 5.6 tons a day of NOx (facts: climate) × the basin's deaths per ton a day from the district's modelling of its 2022 air plan (24.4, 12 to 30): about 137 a year, in line with the advocates' 2,800 over the phase-in.

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: early deaths a year avoided by its NOx cut, once fully in effect
rows.explainer: The district's 0.11 tons a day × the same deaths per ton a day: about 3 a year.

rows.label: EPA's 2024 integrated iron and steel rule: early deaths a year avoided by its fine-particle cut
rows.explainer: From EPA's monetized fine-particle benefits (facts: climate, 20, 8 to 30); its HAP metals' benefits EPA could not quantify, so they count nothing here. The benefit figure includes the illness avoided, so these deaths take no morbidity share on top.

rows.label: Share of each win due to advocacy at all (all groups together)
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.advocacy_share_of_policy_win, 30%, 10% to 60%): the part of a won rule that is the advocates' doing rather than what regulators, courts and deadlines would have brought anyway. The rules are in, so this is not a chance of winning; Industrious Labs' part of the advocates' work is each branch's attribution row.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (docs/normalization.md 2.9).

rows.label: Years from Rule 1146.2 (2024) until its tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: The rule's own dates: units switch when they wear out, from 2026 in new buildings and 2029-2033 in existing ones, over lives of 15 to 25 years, so the middle of the cut is about 2040 (facts: climate, 16 years, 10 to 20).

rows.label: Discount for the wait until Rule 1146.2's tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate; the unit's conversion then discounts the heat deaths from the year the tonne is avoided, so nothing is discounted twice.

rows.label: Discounted years a won reform counts, from the year it takes effect
Rule 1146.2: discounted years of impact
Years from Rule 1153.1 (2023) until its tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: Ovens switch once they are 22 years old (and their burners 7), from 2027, with full implementation by 2043 (the district's report): the middle of the switch about 2035, 12 years after the rule (8 to 16). Our judgment.

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: discounted years of impact
Years from EPA's 2024 steel and coke-oven rules until they take effect
rows.explainer: Compliance was due 2025-2027; a presidential exemption (April 2025) and EPA's interim rule (June 2025) pushed the steel rule's dates back about two years, and the coke-oven rules were restored in October 2025. Our judgment, 3 years from 2024 (2 to 5).

rows.label: EPA's steel rules: discounted years of impact
Rule 1146.2: expected tonnes before adjustments
Rule 1153.1: expected tonnes before adjustments
Expected tonnes a year of the period, before adjustments
rows.explainer: The period's won rules with tonnes, each its tonnes a year × the advocacy share × its discounted years, spread over the period's two years. The campaigns lost or still open in 2023-2024 count at zero against the same spending: DOE's 2024 clean-steel and aluminium awards (SSAB withdrew, DOE dismantled the programme in May 2025, Cleveland-Cliffs moved its Middletown award to coal in 2026), U.S. Steel's Gary blast-furnace reline (2025), Cleveland-Cliffs' Burns Harbor reline (put off three times, not decided), the Colorado and California landfill-methane rules (not adopted in the period), Century Aluminum's planned smelter (its power and award unsettled), and research and community training.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment: how far the per-unit gas and electricity use behind the tonnes should be trusted
rows.explainer: The tonnes are our arithmetic on the district's ex-ante per-unit gas and electricity use (pool heaters run less than assumed in some homes, more in others; the commercial mix is inferred), not measured cuts. The same operating hours drive the owners' fuel bills and the district's NOx cut, so the recurring cost rows and the South Coast deaths take this adjustment too; the units' prices and EPA's steel figures don't. Our judgment, 0.8 (0.5 to 1.1).

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: share of its effects that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this rule (facts: climate, 75%, 50% to 90%): building codes, rebates and the market would have moved some units to heat pumps in the years counted anyway.

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: Industrious Labs' share of the advocates' resources behind it
rows.explainer: Industrious Labs counts Rules 1146.2 and 1153.1 as 'two landmark victories' it secured, organised the first rally for an industrial-boiler rule (Canary Media, 7 June 2024) and intervened to defend the rule with the People's Collective for Environmental Justice and the Sierra Club; Earthjustice was co-counsel, and the Coalition for Clean Air, the Natural Resources Defense Council, RMI and community groups pushed the district's 2022 plan that the rule carries out. Our judgment, 15% (5% to 35%).

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: share of its effects delivered
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate, 70%, 40% to 90%): upheld in district court (2025) and the Ninth Circuit (July 2026), but the 2027 technology review could delay the later dates.

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: share of its effects that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Old gas ovens are rarely replaced by electric ones without a rule; some bakeries electrify for their own climate pledges. Our judgment, 70% (40% to 90%).

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: Industrious Labs' share of the advocates' resources behind it
rows.explainer: A smaller rule with fewer groups behind it: Industrious Labs and Earthjustice made the case for zero-emission ovens with community groups in the district's working groups. Our judgment, 20% (5% to 40%).

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: share of its effects delivered
rows.explainer: Not challenged in court that we found; the zero-emission phase starts in 2027 and ovens can be kept past 22 years with new burners only within the rule's limits. Our judgment, 75% (40% to 90%).

rows.label: EPA's 2024 iron and steel rule: share that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Share of the controls the plants wouldn't have adopted without any rule: spending with no private return, so little would have come anyway. Whether the rule itself would have come later is the shared advocacy share and years a won reform counts, not this row. Our judgment, 90% (70% to 100%).

rows.label: EPA's 2024 iron and steel rule: Industrious Labs' share of the advocates' resources behind it
rows.explainer: Earthjustice litigated for the rule with GASP, the Clean Air Council, the Sierra Club, the Environmental Integrity Project and community groups in Gary and Pittsburgh; Industrious Labs organised steel communities and commented. Our judgment, 5% (2% to 15%).

rows.label: EPA's 2024 iron and steel rule: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: EPA's 2024 iron and steel rule: share of its effects delivered
rows.explainer: A presidential proclamation (April 2025) exempted the mills for two years, EPA's June 2025 interim rule pushed compliance dates back and EPA is reconsidering parts of the rule; it still stands. Our judgment, 40% (15% to 70%).

rows.label: EPA's 2024 coke-oven rules: share that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: Share of the fenceline monitoring and controls the plants wouldn't have adopted without any rule: spending with no private return, so little would have come anyway. Whether the rule itself would have come later is the shared advocacy share and years a won reform counts, not this row. Our judgment, 90% (70% to 100%).

rows.label: EPA's 2024 coke-oven rules: Industrious Labs' share of the advocates' resources behind them
rows.explainer: The same coalition; Industrious Labs' statement on the rules' restoration (9 October 2025) claims part of the win for steel communities. Our judgment, 6% (2% to 15%).

rows.label: EPA's 2024 coke-oven rules: share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: EPA's 2024 coke-oven rules: share delivered
rows.explainer: Exempted by proclamation in 2025 and restored in October 2025 ('Steel Communities Win Back Coke Rules from EPA', Industrious Labs); they may be weakened again. Our judgment, 60% (30% to 85%).

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: The shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12): nothing is measured for Industrious Labs' work; the effects are regulators' estimates and its part a judgment. Every branch takes it.

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: tonnes' adjustments combined
Rule 1153.1: tonnes' adjustments combined
Share of the tonnes that wouldn't have happened anyway (tonnes-weighted, for reading only)
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches with tonnes (weighted by expected tonnes), for reading only; the branches' own rows apply.

rows.label: Industrious Labs' share of the resources behind the tonnes (tonnes-weighted, for reading only)
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches with tonnes, for reading only; the branches' own rows apply, and the EPA branches have their own.

rows.label: Share of credit used (for reading only)
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches with tonnes, for reading only; each branch uses its own share.

rows.label: Share of the tonnes delivered (tonnes-weighted, for reading only)
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches with tonnes, for reading only; the branches' own rows apply, and the EPA branches have their own.

rows.label: All adjustments on the tonnes combined (tonnes-weighted, for reading only)
rows.explainer: The outcome-weighted average of the branches with tonnes, for reading only; the branches' own combined adjustments apply.

rows.label: Side effect: refrigerant leaking from the new heat pumps, as a share of the tonnes
rows.explainer: Heat pumps hold refrigerants that warm the climate when they leak, which the tonnes leave out. For US home heat pumps NREL puts leaks at about 0.07 tonnes a year against 2.5 to 4.4 tonnes cut (facts: climate.us_heat_pump_tco2e_per_household_year, its note), about 2%; a pool heat pump cuts only about 1.3 tonnes a year, so its leaks weigh more, while California limits new units' refrigerants to a warming potential of 750 from 2025. Our judgment, −2% (−6% to 0).

rows.label: Value of a US air-pollution death, units of value (by the ages US air-pollution deaths come at)
rows.explainer: The site's value of a death by age, over the ages of US air-pollution deaths (facts: death_ages, the United States' GBD 2023 mix; moral_weights): these deaths are local, mostly at 70 or older.

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: early deaths avoided by its NOx cut, units of value
rows.formula: s46_nox_deaths_per_year * v_air_death * $life_value_multiplier * evidence_adj * p_success * discounted_years * s46_counterfactual_adj * s46_attribution_share * s46_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The rule's local smog and nitrate deaths, counted directly (the tonnes' own smoke weight is 0, so nothing counts twice), × the evidence adjustment (the district's NOx cut rests on the same operating hours as the gas use), over the same years, wait, advocacy share, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step as its tonnes; × $life_value_multiplier, as every death on the site.

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: early deaths avoided by its NOx cut, units of value
rows.formula: s53_nox_deaths_per_year * v_air_death * $life_value_multiplier * evidence_adj * p_success * s53_discounted_years * s53_counterfactual_adj * s53_attribution_share * s53_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: As for Rule 1146.2.

rows.label: EPA's 2024 iron and steel rule: early deaths avoided, units of value
rows.formula: iis_deaths_per_year * v_air_death * $life_value_multiplier * p_success * epa_discounted_years * iis_counterfactual_adj * iis_attribution_share * iis_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The fine-particle deaths EPA's monetized benefits imply, over the shared years and the rule's wait, with its advocacy share, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step.

rows.label: Real interest rate of the district's low cost case
rows.explainer: The district's two amortization cases are 1% and 4% real; the one-time costs are interpolated between them at the site's discount rate (rows below), so the cost moves with the discount-rate slider.

source.title: South Coast AQMD (May 2024), Draft Socioeconomic Impact Assessment for Proposed Amended Rule 1146.2
source.quote: The average annual compliance costs of PAR 1146.2 are estimated to range from $48.99 million to $96.77 million, depending on the real interest rate assumed (1% to 4%).

rows.label: Real interest rate of the district's high cost case
rows.explainer: As above.

source.title: South Coast AQMD (May 2024), Draft Socioeconomic Impact Assessment for Proposed Amended Rule 1146.2
source.quote: The average annual compliance costs of PAR 1146.2 are estimated to range from $48.99 million to $96.77 million, depending on the real interest rate assumed (1% to 4%).

rows.label: Where the site's discount rate sits between the district's two cases (0 at 1%, 1 at 4%)
rows.explainer: Linear between the two cases and beyond them at the slider's ends (−0.3 at 0.1%, 2.3 at 8%): the amortized capital cost rises about linearly with the rate over 15- to 25-year lives.

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: ovens switched on average over 2024-2051, as a share of all
rows.explainer: The zero-emission phase starts in 2027 and is complete by 2043, so over the district's 2024-2051 window about 60% of the ovens have switched on average (45% to 75%). Our judgment; it scales the district's average costs to full implementation, as the tonnes are counted.

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: units switched on average over 2026-2057, as a share of all

source.title: South Coast AQMD (May 2024), Draft Socioeconomic Impact Assessment for Proposed Amended Rule 1146.2
source.note: Each category's average yearly fuel saving (Table 3) over its per-unit saving (Table 2) gives the units switched in an average year: pool heaters 464,600 of 710,000, tankless water heaters 173,400 of 300,000, other units 38,500 of 60,000; 676,500 of 1,070,000 = 0.63. Range: the categories' own shares, 0.58 to 0.65, widened a little.

rows.explainer: The district's cost is an average over 2026-2057, while units are still being replaced; the tonnes are counted once every unit has switched. Dividing the cost by this share puts both on the same full-implementation footing.

rows.label: Rule 1146.2: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -((@compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1146_2_one_time_cost_1pct + (@compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1146_2_one_time_cost_4pct - @compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1146_2_one_time_cost_1pct) * rate_position) * @compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1146_2_capital_cost_factor + @compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1146_2_recurring_cost * evidence_adj) / scaqmd_phase_in_share * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2023 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * p_success * discounted_years * s46_counterfactual_adj * s46_attribution_share * s46_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21), the district's own analysis: the heat pumps' extra price and panel work, amortized at the site's discount rate (between the district's 1% and 4% cases) × the real-cost factor, plus the owners' fuel-bill change (a saving of $139 million a year on average, × the evidence adjustment, since it rests on the same per-unit use as the tonnes); scaled to full implementation, in 2023 dollars moved to 2024's, valued as money lost by consumers and owners (1.2 times average US consumption), on the log scale; over the same years, wait, advocacy share, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step as the rule's tonnes.

rows.label: Rule 1153.1: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -((@compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1153_1_one_time_cost_1pct + (@compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1153_1_one_time_cost_4pct - @compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1153_1_one_time_cost_1pct) * rate_position) + @compliance_costs.scaqmd_rule_1153_1_recurring_cost * evidence_adj) / s53_phase_in_share * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2023 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * p_success * s53_discounted_years * s53_counterfactual_adj * s53_attribution_share * s53_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: As for Rule 1146.2: the district's one-time costs at the site's rate plus the higher electricity bills ($10.3 million a year on average; electric ovens cost more to run than gas ones), scaled to full implementation.

rows.label: EPA's 2024 iron and steel rule: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_iron_steel_neshap_2024_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2022 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * p_success * epa_discounted_years * iis_counterfactual_adj * iis_attribution_share * iis_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: EPA's estimate, $6.7 million a year (GAO's report of the rule), valued and carried through the branch as above.

rows.label: EPA's 2024 coke-oven rules: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_coke_ovens_neshap_2024_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2023 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * p_success * epa_discounted_years * coke_counterfactual_adj * coke_attribution_share * coke_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: EPA's estimate, $4.0 million a year (2023 dollars), mostly fenceline monitoring. EPA quantified no health benefit, since the rules chiefly keep emissions from rising, so this branch counts only its cost.

rows.label: Side effect: illness avoided by cleaner air (asthma, hospital visits, lost days), as a share of the deaths' value

source.title: South Coast AQMD, 2022 AQMP Socioeconomic Analysis (presented at the REMI users' conference, 2023)
source.page: slide 13, Summary of Public Health Benefits, 2037

rows.explainer: The district's own valuation of its 2022 air plan puts illness avoided at $1.4 billion against $39.1 billion for deaths in 2037: 3.6% (2% to 8%, EPA's analyses often find a little more). Added to the district rules' deaths, not to EPA's steel rule, whose deaths are read off EPA's benefit figure, illness included.

rows.formula: uov_per_year / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)
rows.explainer: Units of value into tonnes at what a tonne of these is worth on the site's scale (its heat and air-pollution deaths by age, as the conversion counts them), the site's bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6).
